title: Migration Gate: Token Bridge, Component Change Control, and Review Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This ticket defines a pragmatic 'Migration Gate' for UI token changes and component surface updates that impact buttons, tables, and charts. The Migration Gate combines: an RFC template, a compatibility assessment, an automated Token Bridge migration shim, a staged rollout plan (canary + cross-team validation), and a formal deprecation schedule.

Scope:
- Visual tokens (color, spacing, type scale, elevation) and token renames/units.
- Component API surface changes that affect markup or behavior for buttons, table cells, and chart series.
- Documentation and demo artifacts (Storybook, design kit).
- Migration shims and fallbacks for client apps.

Non-goals:
- Runtime performance tuning at the kernel level. (Handled by ENG runtime teams.)
- Platform-specific theming beyond token names (platform adaptors are separate).

Principles (design-first, observable, reversible):
1) Preserve behavior: Any change must have a fallback path that preserves current appearance for 90% of consumers during the rollout window.
2) Measure dependency surface: Use usage dashboards to identify consumers and quantify impact before enforcing changes.
3) Ship a bridge: Token renames must include an automated aliasing layer (Token Bridge) and an example migration script.
4) Timebox deprecation: Deprecation windows should be explicit and predictable (default 90 days after final notice unless high-impact).

Migration Gate Phases:
A. RFC + Compatibility Assessment (owners: design + PM + ENG)
  - Draft RFC using the Design System RFC template (link below). Attach a compatibility matrix listing all known consumers and usage counts.
  - Run static scans across repos (scripts/scan-token-usage) and include results.
  - Expected artifact: RFC + compatibility CSV + storybook diff.

B. Bridge Implementation
  - Implement Token Bridge aliasing (CSS tokens, SCSS vars, and JS token map) with feature flag.
  - Add unit and visual regression tests for components referencing affected tokens.
  - Provide migration guide and codemod for common repos.

C. Canary Rollout
  - Enable feature flag for one low-risk internal product, observe visual diffs and error telemetry for 2 weeks.
  - Collect product owner sign-off.

D. Wide Rollout and Deprecation Notice
  - Publish deprecation notice to the Design System changelog, internal slack channel, and partner mail list.
  - After 90 days (or negotiated window), remove old token names from the published package following a final sweep (unless blockers remain).

Review Checklist (must be completed before gate closes):
- RFC completeness: motivation, alternatives, rollback plan, migration plan? (yes/no)
- Compatibility matrix attached and validated (link to CSV and scan).
- Token Bridge implemented and tested with codemod example? (yes/no)
- Visual diff: Storybook snapshots updated and cross-checked with Percy/GH actions? (yes/no)
- Performance & accessibility review: contrast checks, interaction testing on buttons/tables/charts? (yes/no)
- Docs updated: migration guide, changelog entry, release notes drafted? (yes/no)
- Communication plan: owners for notifications and deprecation timeline included? (yes/no)
- Metrics & rollback plan defined: what metric triggers rollback? (e.g., >0.5% visual regressions, new accessibility failures >0)

Reviewers and Approvals:
- Design owner (required).
- Platform/Frontend engineering (required for bridge and codemod).
- Product manager (required for deprecation window).
- DX/Docs (required).
- Optional: Security and Compliance if tokens carry sensitive semantics (e.g., feature flags mapped to back-end behavior).

Artifacts and Templates (links):
- RFC template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/design/rfc-template
- Token usage scanner script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tools/tree/main/token-scanner
- Codemod example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codemods/tree/main/token-rename
- Storybook diff workflow: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/tree/main/storybook-diff
- Migration guide template (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/Design/MigrationGuides/Template

Metrics to collect during rollout:
- Number of repos using deprecated token (per day).
- Visual diffs per PR (percentage and severity).
- Accessibility violations introduced.
- Support tickets referencing visual regressions or broken styles.

Rollback plan:
- Immediate: revert Token Bridge feature flag to preserve old behavior; open emergency PR to revert published package change.
- Follow-up: extend deprecation window, triage consumer breakage, and coordinate fixes with top dependent teams.

Communication cadence:
- RFC announcement: week 0 (internal slack + design changelog).
- Canary results: week 2 (summary doc).
- Wide rollout step-up + deprecation notice: week 4.
- Final removal reminder: 7 days before scheduled removal, then final removal at day 90.

Examples (practical):
- Token rename example: {OLD: 'color-brand-500', NEW: 'color-primary-500'} -> Token Bridge maps aliases so both names resolve. Codemod replaces OLD with NEW over time and PRs flag remaining uses.
- Button prop change: If we rename prop `variant='primary'` to `tone='brand'`, provide a wrapper that maps variant->tone until deprecation window completes.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- RFC created and linked in ticket.
- Token Bridge PoC implemented in the design-tokens package.
- Storybook visual diffs show no high-severity regressions for canary product.
- Migration codemod available and tested in at least two repos.
- Communication draft published and deprecation timeline agreed with stakeholders.

Notes and constraints:
- For high-volume tokens (used in > 20 repos), extend the canary phase and coordinate dedicated migration support.
- For chart primitives, ensure backward-compatible series keys are supported by the chart adapter layer to avoid data-mapping regressions.

Related RFCs and docs attached in comments.
